issue_results.result: Confirmed core derivation error; Major retained. Neither the unconditional lemma nor the main theorem is disproved.
issue_results.source_and_quantifiers: Physical/printed pp11-13: equation(3.10), Definition3.4(1)-(3), the independence assertion before(3.12), and Lemma3.8. Conditioning is on the full incoming crossing-edge configuration E_n, not merely the entrance locations. All nearest-neighbour edges are mandatory with unit conductance. Optional distance-d edges have intensity log(d^2/(d^2-1)), with summable tail.
issue_results.independence_witness: For beta=1/20, alpha=1/4, n=5, j=2, z_1=16 and E_n={(0,1),(0,16)}, all other optional incoming edges absent, the quantile is5: the unconstrained resistance is at most5 and absence of all optional edges incident to its four gap vertices has probability at least2^(-8 beta)>3/4. Conditional events(2),(3) have probabilities (1664/17)^(-beta) and64^(-beta); their allowed edge sets share the16 edges joining9..12 to21..24, with total intensity log(9/8). Joint/product ratio is(9/8)^beta>1. Every optional allowed gap-incident edge joins distinct chain potentials and strictly lowers the maximal chain resistance, so these are exact absence events. The conditioning has positive probability (2N)^(-beta)((256/255)^beta-1). The same z=16,j=2 configuration works for every n>=5, addressing the preceding sufficiently-large-n convention.
issue_results.conditional_quantile_witness: For beta=1/200, alpha=1/4, N=32, E_n={(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(-3,4),(-11,4),(-27,4),(-59,4)} and all other optional incoming crossings absent, the entrance set is{1,2,3,4}. At j=2,3,4,5 the unconditional quantiles are2^j+1 since the lower bound2^(-2*2^j*beta)>3/4. Each exposed edge gives the admissible two-edge path4 -> 5-2^(j+1) -> 4-2^(j+1), of energy2, and forces test(3) to fail. All four tests(1) can hold simultaneously with positive conditional probability, bounded below by exp(-beta*sum_j log(2+5/2^j))=0.9814225497.... M=2.1,L=1.9/log(2.1) give b0=5,b1=1,K_n=1 and eligible i=3. These are admissible displayed scale parameters, not claimed to be the later sufficiently large choices in Proposition3.6.
issue_results.counterevidence_and_boundary: Positive correlation may aid an individual joint lower bound, but does not provide the required conditional marginal bounds or the multi-scale upper failure product. Correcting the printed exponent signs also does not repair this dependence problem. The finite four-scale conditioned event does not refute an unconditional averaged tail bound. No replacement conditional or averaged estimate has been verified.
issue_results.core_dependency: The checked chain is Lemma3.8 -> equation(3.21)/Proposition3.6 -> Proposition3.11 -> Proposition3.2/Theorem3.1 -> Theorem1.1. A demonstrated error in this core derivation warrants Major without a whole-paper counterexample. Exact retained calculations were checked analytically here; their earlier execution is reused, not represented as a new run.

issue_results.decisive_evidence: For every positive integer N, mandatory nearest-neighbour paths0,1,...,N+1 and0,-1,...,-N-1 are edge-disjoint. Removing any one edge leaves at least one exit path. Additional optional edges cannot destroy it. Consequently every such single-edge cut indicator is identically zero, not merely zero in one finite example.

issue_results.source_and_scope: Physical/printed p24 before(4.7), and the direct-exit caveat already acknowledged on p4. Event B controls two truncated resistances and does not itself exclude a direct0-to-exterior edge.
issue_results.decisive_evidence: For N=8, retain optional(0,9), exclude all other optional edges incident to[-8,8], and keep mandatory nearest-neighbour edges. The three parallel paths have resistances9,9,1. Thus R=9/11, the two nonzero-interior exit portions are1/11 each, and the direct portion is9/11. Both truncated side resistances equal their maximum9; the claimed maximum side mass>=1/2 and lower comparison9/4 fail. Because9 is the maximal side resistance, the example is compatible with every attainable threshold in B.
issue_results.repair_and_quantifiers: Let G_N exclude all direct0-to-exterior edges. Its exact probability is(N/(N+1))^(2 beta), so P(G_N^c)<=2 beta/N. Apply each one-sided preceding bound with error epsilon/4, giving joint B failure<=epsilon/2, and take N>=4 beta/epsilon to make G_N failure<=epsilon/2. On B intersect G_N the two-side partition is valid. For finitely many smaller N, R>=1/deg(0)>0 almost surely, since the incident long-edge intensity is finite; finite positive quantiles permit a smaller prefactor. Ordinary point-to-exterior resistance is monotone in N, so its nondyadic extension is valid.
